previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old male with a history of psoriatic arthritis was admitted for severe joint pain and swelling in the left hand and knee, unresponsive to increased oral prednisone. Initial evaluation ruled out infection through negative joint fluid analysis and blood cultures. Imaging showed soft tissue edema and a meniscal tear but no osteonecrosis or abscess. The patient developed bruising on the left knee and shin, which was determined to be inflammatory rather than infectious. He was treated with IV steroids, continued immunosuppressive therapy, and pain management. Symptoms improved gradually, and he was discharged home on a prednisone taper, with increased MS Contin and lidocaine patches, and instructions to follow up with rheumatology.
